en.title: The Suez Canal officially opens
en.text:
On 17 November 1869, a line of ships led by the French imperial yacht L'Aigle, carrying Empress Eugénie, sailed into the new Suez Canal. For the first time, ships could travel from the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea without going all the way around Africa.

The idea was ancient. Pharaohs and later Persian and Arab rulers had dug canals linking the Nile to the Red Sea, but none joined the two seas directly. In 1854 the French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps won a concession from Egypt's ruler Sa'id Pasha, and digging began in April 1859.

The work took ten years. In the early years it relied on forced labour: tens of thousands of Egyptian peasants were made to dig by hand in desert heat, and many died from disease and exhaustion. Later, steam dredgers and excavators did much of the work. The finished canal was about 164 kilometres long, with no locks, because the two seas sit at almost the same level.

The opening was a grand international celebration, with kings, scientists and journalists invited by Khedive Isma'il. Yet the cost pushed Egypt deep into debt. In 1875 Egypt sold its shares to Britain, and in 1882 Britain occupied the country, partly to control the canal.

The canal changed the map of the world. The sea route from London to Mumbai became thousands of kilometres shorter, and ports on the East African coast, from Mombasa to Zanzibar, were suddenly much closer to Europe. That speed also made it easier for European powers to reach, trade with and later colonise Africa and Asia.

In 1956 Egypt's president Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the canal, leading to the Suez Crisis, when Britain, France and Israel invaded and were forced to withdraw under international pressure. The canal was closed again from 1967 to 1975 after war with Israel. Today it has been widened and deepened, and roughly one in ten of the world's traded goods passes through it. When the giant container ship Ever Given got stuck there for six days in 2021, world trade felt the shock.

fr.title: Ouverture officielle du canal de Suez
fr.text: Le canal de Suez est officiellement inauguré en Égypte, reliant la mer Méditerranée à la mer Rouge. Les navires allant d'Europe vers l'Asie et l'Afrique de l'Est n'ont plus besoin de contourner le cap de Bonne-Espérance. Sa construction a duré environ dix ans (1859–1869) et il reste aujourd'hui l'une des routes maritimes les plus importantes du monde.

ar.title: الافتتاح الرسمي لقناة السويس
ar.text: افتُتحت قناة السويس رسميًا في مصر، لتربط البحر الأبيض المتوسط بالبحر الأحمر. ولم تعد السفن المتجهة من أوروبا إلى آسيا وشرق أفريقيا بحاجة إلى الدوران حول رأس الرجاء الصالح. استغرق بناؤها نحو عشر سنوات (1859–1869)، ولا تزال حتى اليوم من أهم طرق الملاحة في العالم.

ko.title: 수에즈 운하 공식 개통
ko.text: 이집트에서 수에즈 운하가 공식 개통되어 지중해와 홍해가 연결되었습니다. 유럽에서 아시아와 동아프리카로 가는 배들은 더 이상 희망봉을 돌아갈 필요가 없게 되었습니다. 건설에는 약 10년(1859–1869)이 걸렸으며, 오늘날에도 세계에서 가장 중요한 해상 항로 중 하나입니다.

ja.title: スエズ運河が正式に開通
ja.text: エジプトでスエズ運河が正式に開通し、地中海と紅海が結ばれました。ヨーロッパからアジアや東アフリカへ向かう船は、もう喜望峰を回る必要がなくなりました。建設には約10年(1859〜1869年)かかり、今も世界で最も重要な航路の一つです。

zh.title: 苏伊士运河正式通航
zh.text: 苏伊士运河在埃及正式通航,连接了地中海和红海。从欧洲前往亚洲和东非的船只不再需要绕行好望角。运河修建历时约十年(1859–1869年),至今仍是世界上最重要的航运通道之一。

es.title: Se inaugura oficialmente el canal de Suez
es.text: El canal de Suez se inauguró oficialmente en Egipto, uniendo el mar Mediterráneo con el mar Rojo. Los barcos que viajaban de Europa a Asia y África Oriental ya no tenían que rodear el cabo de Buena Esperanza. Su construcción duró unos diez años (1859–1869) y hoy sigue siendo una de las rutas marítimas más importantes del mundo.

sw.title: Mfereji wa Suez wafunguliwa rasmi
sw.text: Mfereji wa Suez ulifunguliwa rasmi nchini Misri, ukiunganisha Bahari ya Mediterania na Bahari ya Shamu. Meli kutoka Ulaya kwenda Asia na Afrika Mashariki hazikuhitaji tena kuzunguka Rasi ya Tumaini Jema. Ujenzi wake ulichukua takriban miaka kumi (1859–1869), na hadi leo ni moja ya njia muhimu zaidi za meli duniani.

en.title: Lunokhod 1: the first robot to roam the Moon
en.text:
On 17 November 1970, the Soviet spacecraft Luna 17 landed in the Sea of Rains (Mare Imbrium) on the Moon. A ramp folded down, and an eight-wheeled machine rolled onto the grey dust. Lunokhod 1, whose name means "Moon walker", became the first remote-controlled robot to explore another world.

Lunokhod looked like a bathtub on wheels with a lid. The lid opened in the lunar day to expose solar panels that charged its batteries. During the two-week lunar night, when temperatures fall far below minus 150 °C, the lid closed and a small radioactive heater kept its electronics alive.

There was no autopilot. A team of five drivers sat in a control room in Crimea, nearly 400,000 kilometres away. Every command took several seconds to travel there and back, so they drove slowly, studying a new television picture before each move, always afraid of craters and boulders.

The robot was meant to work for three months. It lasted about ten, until September 1971. It travelled roughly 10.5 kilometres, sent back more than 20,000 pictures and over 200 panoramas, tested the lunar soil at hundreds of places, and studied cosmic rays and X-rays from space.

Lunokhod 1 also carried a laser reflector. For decades scientists could not find it, until in 2010 American researchers located the rover in new orbital photographs and bounced a laser off it again. The little reflector still helps measure the exact distance between Earth and the Moon.

The rover proved that machines could explore other worlds for months, guided from Earth. Every rover that has since rolled across the Moon or Mars, from China's Yutu to NASA's Perseverance, follows the path it opened.

fr.title: Lunokhod 1 : le premier robot à rouler sur la Lune
fr.text: Le Lunokhod 1 de l'Union soviétique se pose sur la Lune à bord de Luna 17 et devient le premier robot à se déplacer à la surface d'un autre monde, piloté depuis la Terre.

ar.title: لونوخود 1: أول روبوت يتجول على سطح القمر
ar.text: هبطت المركبة السوفيتية لونوخود 1 على القمر على متن لونا 17، وأصبحت أول روبوت يتنقل على سطح عالم آخر، يقوده مشغلون من الأرض.

ko.title: 루노호트 1호: 달 표면을 달린 최초의 로봇
ko.text: 소련의 루노호트 1호가 루나 17호에 실려 달에 착륙했고, 지구의 조종사들이 원격으로 움직이며 다른 천체의 표면을 이동한 최초의 로봇이 되었습니다.

ja.title: ルノホート1号:月面を走った初のロボット
ja.text: ソ連のルノホート1号はルナ17号で月に着陸し、地球から操縦されて、地球以外の天体の表面を走行した初のロボットとなりました。

zh.title: 月球车1号:第一个在月球上行驶的机器人
zh.text: 苏联的月球车1号搭乘月球17号登陆月球,在地球上的操作人员遥控下,成为第一个在另一个天体表面行驶的机器人。

es.title: Lunokhod 1: el primer robot que recorrió la Luna
es.text: El Lunokhod 1 de la Unión Soviética llegó a la Luna a bordo de la Luna 17 y se convirtió en el primer robot en recorrer la superficie de otro mundo, guiado por operadores desde la Tierra.

sw.title: Lunokhod 1: roboti ya kwanza kutembea Mwezini
sw.text: Chombo cha Umoja wa Kisovieti, Lunokhod 1, kilitua Mwezini kikiwa ndani ya Luna 17 na kuwa roboti ya kwanza kutembea kwenye uso wa dunia nyingine, kikiongozwa na wataalamu kutoka duniani.

en.title: The origin of International Students' Day
en.text:
International Students' Day is marked around the world on 17 November. It began with tragedy in Prague in 1939, when students paid with their lives for resisting occupation.

In March 1939 Nazi Germany occupied what remained of Czechoslovakia. On 28 October, the anniversary of Czechoslovak independence, crowds in Prague protested. Police and soldiers fired on them. A young medical student, Jan Opletal, was shot in the stomach and died on 11 November.

His funeral on 15 November became another protest, with thousands of students singing the national anthem. The Nazi leadership used it as an excuse to crush the universities. Before dawn on 17 November 1939, troops raided student residences. Nine student leaders and teachers were executed without trial. Around 1,200 students were sent to the Sachsenhausen concentration camp, and all Czech universities and colleges were closed for the rest of the war.

In 1941, students who had escaped to London, together with the International Students' Council, declared 17 November International Students' Day, to honour the victims and to stand for the right to education and freedom.

The date returned to history fifty years later. On 17 November 1989 students in Prague marched to remember 1939. Riot police beat them, and the anger that followed grew into the peaceful Velvet Revolution, which ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia within weeks.

Today the day is used by student unions worldwide to talk about access to education, free speech and student welfare. It is a reminder that young people in classrooms have often been the first to stand up when freedom is threatened.

fr.title: Origine de la Journée internationale des étudiants
fr.text: Neuf étudiants tchèques sont exécutés par le régime nazi après des manifestations. Cet événement est devenu l'origine de la Journée internationale des étudiants, célébrée chaque 17 novembre.

ar.title: أصل اليوم العالمي للطلاب
ar.text: أعدم النظام النازي تسعة طلاب تشيكيين بعد احتجاجات. وأصبح هذا الحدث لاحقًا أصل اليوم العالمي للطلاب الذي يُحتفل به في 17 نوفمبر من كل عام.

ko.title: 국제 학생의 날의 기원
ko.text: 시위 이후 체코 학생 9명이 나치 정권에 의해 처형되었습니다. 이 사건은 훗날 매년 11월 17일에 기념하는 국제 학생의 날의 기원이 되었습니다.

ja.title: 国際学生の日の始まり
ja.place: チェコスロバキア・プラハ
ja.text: 抗議活動の後、チェコの学生9人がナチス政権によって処刑されました。この出来事が、毎年11月17日に記念される国際学生の日の始まりとなりました。

zh.title: 国际学生日的由来
zh.text: 抗议活动之后,九名捷克学生被纳粹政权处决。这一事件后来成为国际学生日的由来,每年11月17日纪念。

es.title: Origen del Día Internacional de los Estudiantes
es.text: Nueve estudiantes checos fueron ejecutados por el régimen nazi tras unas protestas. Este hecho dio origen al Día Internacional de los Estudiantes, que se celebra cada 17 de noviembre.

sw.title: Chanzo cha Siku ya Kimataifa ya Wanafunzi
sw.text: Wanafunzi tisa wa Kicheki waliuawa na utawala wa Kinazi baada ya maandamano. Tukio hili baadaye likawa chanzo cha Siku ya Kimataifa ya Wanafunzi, inayoadhimishwa kila tarehe 17 Novemba.

en.title: Tanganyika gains independence
en.text:
At midnight on 9 December 1961, in a packed stadium in Dar es Salaam, the British flag was lowered in darkness and the green, black and gold flag of Tanganyika was raised. After more than seventy years of colonial rule, Tanganyika was free.

The road began long before. From the 1880s the territory was part of German East Africa. After Germany's defeat in the First World War, Britain ruled it under a League of Nations mandate and later as a United Nations trust territory. That status mattered: the United Nations sent visiting missions, and Tanganyikans could petition the world body directly.

In 1954 a young teacher named Julius Kambarage Nyerere helped turn the Tanganyika African Association into a political party, TANU. Travelling across the country by bus, bicycle and on foot, TANU organisers built support in towns and villages. Nyerere spoke at the United Nations in New York in 1955, calmly arguing that Tanganyikans were ready to govern themselves.

Unlike many independence struggles, Tanganyika's was achieved without war. TANU won the elections of 1958–59 and 1960 by huge margins. Self-government came in 1961, then full independence on 9 December, with Nyerere as prime minister.

On the same night, army officer Alexander Nyirenda planted the national flag and lit a torch on the summit of Kilimanjaro. Nyerere had said the country would light a candle on the mountain that would shine beyond its borders, bringing hope where there was despair. The Uhuru Torch still runs across the country each year.

Exactly one year later, on 9 December 1962, Tanganyika became a republic with Nyerere as its first president. In 1964 it united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania. Independence Day, 9 December, remains one of the country's most important national days.

fr.title: Le Tanganyika obtient son indépendance
fr.text: Le Tanganyika obtient son indépendance du Royaume-Uni, avec Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere comme Premier ministre. Un an plus tard, le Tanganyika devient une république, avec Nyerere comme premier président.

ar.title: تنجانيقا تنال استقلالها
ar.text: نالت تنجانيقا استقلالها عن بريطانيا، وتولّى المعلم جوليوس كامباراجي نيريري رئاسة الوزراء. وبعد عام أصبحت تنجانيقا جمهورية، وكان نيريري أول رئيس لها.

ko.title: 탕가니카 독립
ko.text: 탕가니카가 영국으로부터 독립했고, 므왈리무 줄리어스 캄바라게 니에레레가 총리가 되었습니다. 1년 뒤 탕가니카는 공화국이 되었고 니에레레가 초대 대통령이 되었습니다.

ja.title: タンガニーカが独立
ja.text: タンガニーカがイギリスから独立し、ムワリム・ジュリウス・カンバラゲ・ニエレレが首相に就任しました。1年後、タンガニーカは共和国となり、ニエレレが初代大統領となりました。

zh.title: 坦噶尼喀独立
zh.text: 坦噶尼喀脱离英国获得独立,姆瓦利姆·朱利叶斯·坎巴拉吉·尼雷尔出任总理。一年后,坦噶尼喀成为共和国,尼雷尔成为首任总统。

es.title: Tanganica obtiene su independencia
es.text: Tanganica obtuvo su independencia del Reino Unido, con Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere como primer ministro. Un año después, Tanganica se convirtió en república, con Nyerere como su primer presidente.

sw.title: Tanganyika yapata uhuru
sw.text: Tanganyika ilipata uhuru wake kutoka kwa Uingereza, na Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere akawa Waziri Mkuu. Mwaka mmoja baadaye Tanganyika ikawa Jamhuri, Nyerere akiwa Rais wake wa kwanza.

en.title: The Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
en.text:
On 26 April 1964, two independent countries became one. Tanganyika on the mainland and Zanzibar, the islands of Unguja and Pemba, joined to form the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. In October that year the new country took the name Tanzania, built from TANganyika, ZANzibar and the hope of something new.

The two lands were already joined by geography, language and history. For centuries traders, fishermen and families had crossed the narrow channel. Kiswahili was spoken on both sides, and the caravan routes from the interior ended at coastal towns facing the islands.

Zanzibar had gained independence from Britain in December 1963, then experienced a revolution in January 1964 that brought Abeid Amani Karume and the Afro-Shirazi Party to power. Cold War tensions were high, and leaders on both sides wanted security and unity.

On 22 April 1964, President Julius Nyerere and President Karume signed the Articles of Union. Four days later the union came into force. Nyerere became president of the United Republic, and Karume became first vice-president. Zanzibar kept its own government and president for matters that were not union affairs, an arrangement that still exists today.

The union is one of the few lasting political unions of independent African states. It has been debated many times, about how powers and revenues are shared, but it has endured for more than sixty years.

Union Day, 26 April, is a public holiday in Tanzania. The mixing of soil from Tanganyika and Zanzibar, performed by the two presidents in 1964, remains a powerful symbol of a nation built by choice.

fr.title: Union du Tanganyika et de Zanzibar
fr.text: Le Tanganyika et Zanzibar s'unissent pour former la République unie, nommée Tanzanie plus tard la même année. Ce jour est célébré chaque année comme la Journée de l'Union.

ar.title: اتحاد تنجانيقا وزنجبار
ar.text: اتحدت تنجانيقا وزنجبار لتشكيل الجمهورية المتحدة، التي سُمّيت تنزانيا في وقت لاحق من العام نفسه. ويُحتفل بهذا اليوم سنويًا باسم يوم الاتحاد.

ko.title: 탕가니카와 잔지바르의 통합
ko.text: 탕가니카와 잔지바르가 통합하여 연합공화국을 세웠고, 같은 해 말 탄자니아라는 이름을 갖게 되었습니다. 이날은 매년 연합의 날로 기념됩니다.

ja.title: タンガニーカとザンジバルの連合

ja.text: タンガニーカとザンジバルが統合して連合共和国が誕生し、同じ年のうちにタンザニアと名付けられました。この日は毎年「連合の日」として祝われています。

zh.title: 坦噶尼喀与桑给巴尔联合
zh.text: 坦噶尼喀与桑给巴尔联合组成联合共和国,并于同年晚些时候定名为坦桑尼亚。每年这一天都作为联合日庆祝。

es.title: Unión de Tanganica y Zanzíbar
es.text: Tanganica y Zanzíbar se unieron para formar la República Unida, que ese mismo año recibió el nombre de Tanzania. Este día se celebra cada año como el Día de la Unión.

sw.title: Muungano wa Tanganyika na Zanzibar
sw.text: Tanganyika na Zanzibar ziliungana na kuunda Jamhuri ya Muungano, ambayo baadaye mwaka huo huo ilipewa jina Tanzania. Siku hii huadhimishwa kila mwaka kama Siku ya Muungano.

en.title: The Zanzibar Revolution
en.text:
In the early hours of 12 January 1964, armed revolutionaries attacked police stations and armouries in Zanzibar town. Within a day the government of the Sultan of Zanzibar had collapsed. The Sultan, Jamshid bin Abdullah, fled by ship, and Zanzibar became a people's republic.

The revolution grew out of deep divisions. For generations, power and much of the best land on the islands had been held by an Arab ruling class under the Sultanate, while the African majority, many of them descendants of people brought to the islands in the slave trade, had far less wealth and political influence.

When Britain granted independence on 10 December 1963, Zanzibar became a constitutional monarchy under the Sultan. Elections had given most votes to the Afro-Shirazi Party (ASP), yet the way seats were drawn left a coalition of other parties in government. Many Africans felt independence had changed little.

The uprising itself was led in its first hours by a small armed group, including the Ugandan-born John Okello. Abeid Amani Karume, leader of the ASP, became president of the new People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba. The revolutionary government took over large estates and began programmes in housing, schools and health care.

The revolution was also violent. Thousands of people, many of them of Arab and South Asian descent, were killed or forced to flee in the following days. Historians still debate the numbers, and the memory is painful for many families.

Three months later Zanzibar joined Tanganyika to form Tanzania. Revolution Day, Mapinduzi Day, is celebrated every 12 January on the islands. It marks a turning point that changed who held power in Zanzibar and shaped the islands' place in the union.

fr.title: Révolution de Zanzibar
fr.text: La révolution renverse le pouvoir du sultan de Zanzibar. Ce jour est célébré chaque année comme la Journée de la révolution de Zanzibar.

ar.title: ثورة زنجبار
ar.text: أطاحت الثورة بحكم سلطان زنجبار. ويُحتفل بهذا اليوم سنويًا باسم يوم ثورة زنجبار.

ko.title: 잔지바르 혁명
ko.text: 혁명으로 잔지바르 술탄의 통치가 무너졌습니다. 이날은 매년 잔지바르 혁명 기념일로 기념됩니다.

ja.title: ザンジバル革命
ja.text: 革命によってザンジバルのスルタンの支配が倒されました。この日は毎年「ザンジバル革命記念日」として祝われています。

zh.title: 桑给巴尔革命
zh.text: 革命推翻了桑给巴尔苏丹的统治。每年这一天都作为桑给巴尔革命纪念日庆祝。

es.title: Revolución de Zanzíbar
es.text: La revolución derrocó el gobierno del sultán de Zanzíbar. Este día se celebra cada año como el Día de la Revolución de Zanzíbar.

sw.title: Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar
sw.text: Mapinduzi yaliuondoa utawala wa Sultani wa Zanzibar. Siku hii huadhimishwa kila mwaka kama Siku ya Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar.

en.title: The founding of TANU
en.text:
On 7 July 1954, a meeting in Dar es Salaam transformed the Tanganyika African Association, a mostly social and civil-service organisation, into a political party: the Tanganyika African National Union, TANU. Its president was a 32-year-old teacher, Julius Nyerere.

TANU had one clear goal: self-government leading to independence. It also insisted that independence should belong to all the peoples of Tanganyika, whatever their ethnic group, religion or race. That message of unity was powerful in a country with more than 120 ethnic groups.

The party grew quickly because it was organised from the grassroots. Members paid small dues and received cards. Branches formed in towns and villages, and women such as Bibi Titi Mohammed mobilised thousands of women into the movement, becoming some of its strongest organisers.

TANU used Kiswahili as its language of politics. Speeches, songs and newspapers in a shared language helped people from every region feel part of one national struggle, and Kiswahili later became the national language.

British officials tried to limit TANU, banning some branches and restricting meetings. But in the elections of 1958–59 and 1960 TANU-backed candidates won almost every seat. Independence followed in December 1961.

In 1977 TANU merged with Zanzibar's Afro-Shirazi Party to form Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM). The founding day, 7 July, Saba Saba (seven seven), is remembered in Tanzania and gave its name to the famous Dar es Salaam International Trade Fair held every year around that date.

fr.title: Fondation de la TANU
fr.text: La TANU (Tanganyika African National Union) est fondée sous la direction de Julius Nyerere. Le parti mène la lutte pour l'indépendance du Tanganyika. C'est l'origine de la journée de Saba Saba.

ar.title: تأسيس حزب تانو
ar.text: تأسس حزب تانو (الاتحاد الوطني الأفريقي لتنجانيقا) بقيادة جوليوس نيريري. وقاد الحزب النضال من أجل استقلال تنجانيقا، ومنه نشأ يوم «سابا سابا».

ko.title: TANU 창당
ko.text: 줄리어스 니에레레의 지도 아래 TANU(탕가니카 아프리카 민족연합)가 창당되었습니다. 이 정당은 탕가니카 독립운동을 이끌었으며, '사바 사바' 기념일의 기원이 되었습니다.

ja.title: TANUの結成
ja.text: ジュリウス・ニエレレの指導のもと、TANU(タンガニーカ・アフリカ民族同盟)が結成されました。この政党はタンガニーカ独立運動を率い、「サバ・サバ」の日の由来となりました。

zh.title: 坦盟(TANU)成立
zh.text: 在朱利叶斯·尼雷尔的领导下,坦噶尼喀非洲民族联盟(TANU)成立。该党领导了坦噶尼喀的独立运动,也是“萨巴萨巴”节的由来。

es.title: Fundación de la TANU
es.text: La TANU (Tanganyika African National Union) se fundó bajo el liderazgo de Julius Nyerere. El partido encabezó la lucha por la independencia de Tanganica. Es el origen del día de Saba Saba.

sw.title: Kuanzishwa kwa chama cha TANU
sw.text: Chama cha TANU (Tanganyika African National Union) kilianzishwa chini ya uongozi wa Julius Nyerere. Chama hiki kiliongoza harakati za kudai uhuru wa Tanganyika. Ndiyo asili ya Siku ya Saba Saba.

en.title: The death of Mwalimu Julius Nyerere
en.text:
On 14 October 1999, Julius Kambarage Nyerere, the founding father of Tanzania, died of leukaemia in St Thomas' Hospital in London. He was 77. Tanzanians, and many people across Africa, mourned him as Mwalimu, the Teacher.

Nyerere was born in 1922 in Butiama, near Lake Victoria, son of a Zanaki chief. He studied at Makerere College in Uganda, became a teacher, and then studied history and economics at the University of Edinburgh, one of the first Tanganyikans to study at a British university.

He led TANU to independence without war in 1961 and became Tanzania's first president. He promoted Kiswahili as a national language, which helped unite more than a hundred ethnic groups. Tanzania became known for peace and stability in a troubled region.

In the 1967 Arusha Declaration he set out his idea of Ujamaa, African socialism built on family-hood, self-reliance and equality. Schools and clinics spread widely and literacy rose sharply. But forced villagisation and state control of the economy also brought hardship, and the economy struggled by the 1980s. Nyerere openly admitted mistakes.

Abroad, he was a leading voice against colonialism and apartheid. Dar es Salaam hosted liberation movements from Mozambique, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Namibia and Angola. In 1978–79 Tanzania fought back against Idi Amin's invasion and helped end his rule in Uganda.

In 1985 Nyerere stepped down voluntarily, rare among leaders of his era. He also translated Shakespeare's Julius Caesar and The Merchant of Venice into Kiswahili. His body was returned home and buried in Butiama. Nyerere Day, 14 October, is a national holiday.

fr.title: Décès de Mwalimu Julius Nyerere
fr.text: Le Père de la Nation, Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere, meurt à Londres. Cette date est commémorée en Tanzanie comme la Journée de Mwalimu Nyerere.

ar.title: وفاة المعلم جوليوس نيريري
ar.text: توفي أبو الأمة، المعلم جوليوس كامباراجي نيريري، في لندن. وتُحيي تنزانيا هذا التاريخ باسم يوم المعلم نيريري.

ko.title: 므왈리무 줄리어스 니에레레 서거
ko.text: 국부 므왈리무 줄리어스 캄바라게 니에레레가 런던에서 세상을 떠났습니다. 탄자니아에서는 이날을 므왈리무 니에레레의 날로 기념합니다.

ja.title: ムワリム・ジュリウス・ニエレレの死去
ja.text: 建国の父ムワリム・ジュリウス・カンバラゲ・ニエレレがロンドンで亡くなりました。タンザニアではこの日を「ムワリム・ニエレレの日」として記念しています。

zh.title: 姆瓦利姆·朱利叶斯·尼雷尔逝世
zh.text: 国父姆瓦利姆·朱利叶斯·坎巴拉吉·尼雷尔在伦敦逝世。坦桑尼亚将这一天定为“尼雷尔纪念日”。

es.title: Muerte de Mwalimu Julius Nyerere
es.text: El Padre de la Nación, Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere, falleció en Londres. Esta fecha se conmemora en Tanzania como el Día de Mwalimu Nyerere.

sw.title: Kifo cha Mwalimu Julius Nyerere
sw.text: Baba wa Taifa, Mwalimu Julius Kambarage Nyerere, alifariki dunia jijini London. Tarehe hii huadhimishwa Tanzania kama Siku ya Mwalimu Nyerere.

en.title: The summit of Kilimanjaro is reached
en.text:
On 6 October 1889, three men stood on the highest point of Kilimanjaro, the roof of Africa, after a long climb across ice. They were the German geologist Hans Meyer, the Austrian mountaineer Ludwig Purtscheller, and their local guide from Marangu, Yohani Kinyala Lauwo.

Kilimanjaro rises 5,895 metres above sea level. It is the highest mountain in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain on Earth. It is a huge volcano with three cones: Kibo, the highest; jagged Mawenzi; and the old, worn Shira plateau.

For the Chagga people living on its fertile slopes, the mountain was home, a source of water and a place woven into their stories. Europeans long refused to believe reports, first written in 1848 by the missionary Johannes Rebmann, of a snow-covered mountain so near the equator.

Meyer had failed on two earlier attempts. In 1889 the team climbed with porters and Lauwo's guidance, setting up camps on the way. On the summit Meyer named the highest point Kaiser-Wilhelm-Spitze after the German emperor. Lauwo, who was still in his teens at the time, went on to guide climbers for decades; Tanzania later honoured his role.

At independence in 1961 the summit was renamed Uhuru Peak, Freedom Peak, and the Uhuru Torch was lit there.

Today more than 30,000 people try to climb Kilimanjaro each year, most guided and supported by Tanzanian guides and porters. Its famous glaciers, however, are shrinking quickly. Scientists warn that most of the ice that has crowned the mountain for thousands of years could disappear within decades.

fr.title: Le sommet du Kilimandjaro est atteint
fr.text: Hans Meyer et Ludwig Purtscheller atteignent le sommet Kibo du Kilimandjaro, la plus haute montagne d'Afrique. C'est la première ascension du sommet attestée.

ar.title: الوصول إلى قمة كليمنجارو
ar.text: وصل هانز ماير ولودفيغ بورتشيلر إلى قمة كيبو في جبل كليمنجارو، أعلى جبل في أفريقيا. وكان ذلك أول صعود مسجَّل إلى القمة.

ko.title: 킬리만자로 정상 등정
ko.text: 한스 마이어와 루트비히 푸르첼러가 아프리카 최고봉인 킬리만자로산의 키보 정상에 올랐습니다. 이는 기록으로 남은 최초의 정상 등정이었습니다.

ja.title: キリマンジャロ山頂に到達
ja.place: タンザニア・キリマンジャロ
ja.text: ハンス・マイヤーとルートヴィヒ・プルトシェラーが、アフリカ最高峰キリマンジャロのキボ峰山頂に到達しました。記録に残る初の登頂でした。

zh.title: 登顶乞力马扎罗山
zh.text: 汉斯·迈耶和路德维希·普尔切勒登上了非洲最高峰乞力马扎罗山的基博峰顶。这是有记录的首次登顶。

es.title: Se alcanza la cima del Kilimanjaro
es.text: Hans Meyer y Ludwig Purtscheller llegaron a la cima Kibo del Kilimanjaro, la montaña más alta de África. Fue el primer ascenso registrado a la cumbre.

sw.title: Kilele cha Kilimanjaro chafikiwa
sw.text: Hans Meyer na Ludwig Purtscheller walifika kilele cha Kibo cha Mlima Kilimanjaro, mlima mrefu zaidi barani Afrika. Ni mara ya kwanza iliyorekodiwa kwa wapandaji kufika kileleni.

en.title: The Organisation of African Unity is founded
en.text:
On 25 May 1963, leaders of 32 independent African states gathered in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, and signed the charter of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU). It was the first organisation to bring almost the whole of independent Africa together.

The meeting was hosted by Emperor Haile Selassie. It included leaders such as Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana, Julius Nyerere of Tanganyika, Sékou Touré of Guinea, Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt and Modibo Keïta of Mali.

The leaders disagreed about how far unity should go. Nkrumah wanted a full union of African states with one government. Others preferred cooperation between sovereign countries. The OAU took the second path, but it agreed on shared goals: defend independence, improve life for Africans, and free the continent from colonialism and apartheid.

The OAU's Liberation Committee was based in Dar es Salaam. It channelled money, training and support to liberation movements fighting in Mozambique, Angola, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Guinea-Bissau and South Africa.

The OAU also accepted the borders left by colonial powers, to avoid endless wars over territory, and insisted on non-interference in members' internal affairs. Critics later said this let some governments abuse their people without challenge.

In 2002 the OAU was replaced by the African Union, which has stronger powers to act in crises. The founding date, 25 May, is celebrated each year as Africa Day across the continent and among Africans around the world.

fr.title: Fondation de l'Organisation de l'unité africaine (OUA)
fr.text: Les dirigeants des États africains indépendants fondent l'OUA, ancêtre de l'Union africaine (UA). Cette date est aujourd'hui célébrée comme la Journée de l'Afrique.

ar.title: تأسيس منظمة الوحدة الأفريقية
ar.text: أسس قادة الدول الأفريقية المستقلة منظمة الوحدة الأفريقية، التي سبقت الاتحاد الأفريقي. ويُحتفل بهذا التاريخ اليوم باسم يوم أفريقيا.

ko.title: 아프리카 통일기구(OAU) 창설
ko.text: 독립한 아프리카 국가들의 지도자들이 아프리카연합(AU)의 전신인 OAU를 창설했습니다. 이날은 오늘날 아프리카의 날로 기념됩니다.

ja.title: アフリカ統一機構(OAU)の設立
ja.place: エチオピア・アディスアベバ
ja.text: 独立したアフリカ諸国の指導者たちが、アフリカ連合(AU)の前身であるOAUを設立しました。この日は現在「アフリカの日」として祝われています。

zh.title: 非洲统一组织(OAU)成立
zh.place: 埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴
zh.text: 独立的非洲国家领导人成立了非洲统一组织,即非洲联盟(AU)的前身。这一天如今被定为“非洲日”。

es.title: Fundación de la Organización para la Unidad Africana (OUA)
es.text: Los líderes de los Estados africanos independientes fundaron la OUA, predecesora de la Unión Africana (UA). Esta fecha se celebra hoy como el Día de África.

sw.title: Kuanzishwa kwa Umoja wa Nchi Huru za Afrika (OAU)
sw.text: Viongozi wa nchi huru za Afrika walianzisha OAU, chombo kilichotangulia Umoja wa Afrika (AU). Tarehe hii sasa huadhimishwa kama Siku ya Afrika.

en.title: Nelson Mandela is released
en.place: Paarl and Cape Town, South Africa
en.text:
On the afternoon of 11 February 1990, Nelson Mandela walked out of the gates of Victor Verster Prison near Paarl, holding hands with his wife Winnie, and raised his fist. He had been in prison for 27 years. Television carried the moment to the whole world.

Mandela, born in 1918 in the Eastern Cape, was a lawyer and a leader of the African National Congress (ANC). He fought apartheid, the system of laws that separated South Africans by race and denied the Black majority the vote, good land, and freedom of movement.

After the ANC was banned in 1960, Mandela helped form its armed wing. Arrested in 1962, he was tried with other leaders in the Rivonia Trial. In 1964 he told the court that a democratic, free society was an ideal for which he was prepared to die. He was sentenced to life imprisonment.

He spent 18 years on Robben Island, breaking rocks in a lime quarry, then years in other prisons. His name became a worldwide symbol, and campaigns, boycotts and sanctions pressured the apartheid government.

On 2 February 1990, President F. W. de Klerk announced the unbanning of the ANC and other movements. Nine days later Mandela was free. That evening he spoke from the balcony of Cape Town City Hall to a huge crowd, calling for continued struggle and for peace.

Negotiations followed, through years of violence. In April 1994 South Africa held its first election in which all citizens could vote, and Mandela became president. He and de Klerk shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993. Mandela died in 2013, honoured as one of the great peacemakers of history.

fr.title: Nelson Mandela est libéré
fr.text: Nelson Mandela est libéré après 27 ans de prison. Quatre ans plus tard, il devient le premier président de l'Afrique du Sud élu lors d'une élection pleinement démocratique.

ar.title: الإفراج عن نيلسون مانديلا
ar.text: أُفرج عن نيلسون مانديلا بعد 27 عامًا في السجن. وبعد أربع سنوات أصبح أول رئيس لجنوب أفريقيا يُنتخب في انتخابات ديمقراطية شاملة.

ko.title: 넬슨 만델라 석방
ko.text: 넬슨 만델라가 27년간의 수감 생활 끝에 석방되었습니다. 4년 뒤 그는 완전한 민주 선거로 선출된 남아프리카공화국 최초의 대통령이 되었습니다.

ja.title: ネルソン・マンデラが釈放される
ja.text: ネルソン・マンデラが27年間の獄中生活を経て釈放されました。4年後、彼は完全な民主選挙で選ばれた南アフリカ初の大統領となりました。

zh.title: 纳尔逊·曼德拉获释
zh.text: 纳尔逊·曼德拉在狱中度过27年后获释。四年后,他成为南非首位通过全面民主选举产生的总统。

es.title: Nelson Mandela es liberado
es.text: Nelson Mandela fue liberado tras 27 años en prisión. Cuatro años después se convirtió en el primer presidente de Sudáfrica elegido en unas elecciones plenamente democráticas.

sw.title: Nelson Mandela aachiliwa huru
sw.text: Nelson Mandela aliachiliwa huru baada ya miaka 27 gerezani. Miaka minne baadaye akawa Rais wa kwanza wa Afrika Kusini kuchaguliwa katika uchaguzi wa kidemokrasia wa watu wote.

en.title: Ghana gains independence
en.text:
At midnight on 6 March 1957, at the Old Polo Grounds in Accra, Kwame Nkrumah stood before a cheering crowd and declared that Ghana was free forever. The British colony of the Gold Coast became Ghana, one of the first countries in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule.

The name Ghana was chosen on purpose. It recalled the ancient empire of Ghana, or Wagadu, a rich West African kingdom known for gold, which flourished more than a thousand years earlier, to the north-west of the modern country.

The Gold Coast had been ruled by Britain since the nineteenth century, after long resistance including the Anglo-Asante wars. After the Second World War, returning soldiers, farmers angry about low cocoa prices, and educated young people demanded change. Riots in 1948 shook the colonial government.

Nkrumah, who had studied in the United States and Britain, founded the Convention People's Party in 1949 and called for "self-government now". He was jailed for organising strikes, but his party won elections while he was in prison, and he was released to lead the government.

In his independence speech, Nkrumah said that Ghana's freedom would be meaningless unless it was linked to the total liberation of Africa. Ghana's black star flag became a symbol for the whole continent, and Accra hosted meetings of African liberation movements.

Nkrumah was overthrown in a coup in 1966 and Ghana went through difficult decades. Since 1992 it has held regular democratic elections. 6 March remains Ghana's Independence Day, and the date is seen as the moment a wave of African independence began.

fr.title: Le Ghana obtient son indépendance
fr.text: Le Ghana, dirigé par Kwame Nkrumah, obtient son indépendance du Royaume-Uni et devient un exemple pour les mouvements d'indépendance de toute l'Afrique.

ar.title: غانا تنال استقلالها
ar.text: نالت غانا، بقيادة كوامي نكروما، استقلالها عن بريطانيا، وأصبحت قدوة لحركات الاستقلال في جميع أنحاء أفريقيا.

ko.title: 가나 독립
ko.text: 콰메 은크루마가 이끄는 가나가 영국으로부터 독립하여 아프리카 전역의 독립운동에 본보기가 되었습니다.

ja.title: ガーナが独立
ja.text: クワメ・エンクルマ率いるガーナがイギリスから独立し、アフリカ各地の独立運動の模範となりました。

zh.title: 加纳独立
zh.text: 在克瓦米·恩克鲁玛的领导下,加纳脱离英国获得独立,成为整个非洲独立运动的榜样。

es.title: Ghana obtiene su independencia
es.text: Ghana, liderada por Kwame Nkrumah, obtuvo su independencia del Reino Unido y se convirtió en un ejemplo para los movimientos de independencia de toda África.

sw.title: Ghana yapata uhuru
sw.text: Ghana, chini ya uongozi wa Kwame Nkrumah, ilipata uhuru kutoka kwa Uingereza na kuwa mfano kwa harakati za uhuru kote barani Afrika.

en.title: Humans walk on the Moon
en.text:
On 20 July 1969, the lunar module Eagle landed on a flat plain on the Moon called the Sea of Tranquillity. Hours later, Neil Armstrong climbed down the ladder and became the first human being to step onto another world.

Apollo 11 launched from Florida on 16 July on a giant Saturn V rocket. On board were three American astronauts: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins. Collins stayed in orbit in the command module Columbia while Armstrong and Aldrin flew Eagle down to the surface.

The landing was dangerous. Computer alarms sounded, and the planned site was full of boulders, so Armstrong flew on by hand and landed with very little fuel left. His first words from the surface were that Tranquility Base was here and the Eagle had landed.

Armstrong and Aldrin spent about two and a half hours walking outside. They planted a flag, set up experiments including a laser reflector and a seismometer, and collected 21.5 kilograms of rocks and soil. An estimated 600 million people watched on television, one of the largest audiences in history.

The mission was the high point of the space race between the United States and the Soviet Union, which had already sent the first satellite and the first human into space. Thousands of engineers, scientists and mathematicians worked on Apollo, including Black women mathematicians such as Katherine Johnson, whose calculations were crucial to the programme.

The crew returned safely on 24 July. Between 1969 and 1972, twelve astronauts walked on the Moon. No one has returned since, but new missions plan to take humans back.

fr.title: L'homme marche sur la Lune
fr.text: Neil Armstrong et Buzz Aldrin, de la mission Apollo 11, deviennent les premiers êtres humains à marcher sur la Lune, tandis que Michael Collins reste en orbite dans le module de commande.

ar.title: الإنسان يمشي على القمر
ar.text: أصبح نيل أرمسترونغ وباز ألدرين من مهمة أبولو 11 أول إنسانين يمشيان على سطح القمر، بينما كان مايكل كولينز يدور حول القمر في وحدة القيادة.

ko.title: 인류, 달에 발을 딛다
ko.text: 아폴로 11호의 닐 암스트롱과 버즈 올드린이 달 위를 걸은 최초의 인류가 되었고, 마이클 콜린스는 사령선을 타고 달 궤도를 돌았습니다.

ja.title: 人類が月面を歩く
ja.text: アポロ11号のニール・アームストロングとバズ・オルドリンが月面を歩いた最初の人類となり、マイケル・コリンズは司令船で月の周回軌道を回りました。

zh.title: 人类登上月球
zh.text: 阿波罗11号的尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·奥尔德林成为首批在月球上行走的人类,迈克尔·柯林斯则驾驶指令舱环绕月球飞行。

es.title: El ser humano pisa la Luna
es.text: Neil Armstrong y Buzz Aldrin, del Apolo 11, se convirtieron en los primeros seres humanos en pisar la Luna, mientras Michael Collins orbitaba la Luna en el módulo de mando.

sw.title: Binadamu wakanyaga Mwezi
sw.text: Neil Armstrong na Buzz Aldrin wa chombo Apollo 11 wakawa binadamu wa kwanza kukanyaga Mwezi, huku Michael Collins akizunguka Mwezi ndani ya chombo kikuu.

en.title: The first human in space
en.text:
On the morning of 12 April 1961, a 27-year-old Soviet pilot named Yuri Gagarin lay strapped inside a small round capsule called Vostok 1. As the rocket lifted off from Baikonur, in today's Kazakhstan, he called out "Poyekhali!", "Let's go!" He was about to become the first human being in space.

Gagarin was the son of a carpenter and a dairy worker from a village west of Moscow. He trained as a foundry worker, joined a flying club, and became a fighter pilot. Out of thousands of candidates, he was chosen partly for his calm nature and his small size, which suited the cramped capsule.

The flight lasted 108 minutes. Gagarin circled the Earth once, travelling at about 27,000 kilometres per hour. He reported what he saw: the curve of the planet, the blue band of the atmosphere, the darkness of space. The capsule was controlled from the ground, since no one yet knew how a human would cope with weightlessness.

On the way down, at about seven kilometres above the ground, Gagarin ejected from the capsule as planned and landed by parachute in a field near the Volga River. A farmer and her granddaughter were the first people to meet him.

His flight shocked the United States and sped up the space race, leading President Kennedy to set the goal of reaching the Moon. Gagarin became a hero across the world, visiting many countries.

He died in 1968 in a training jet crash. 12 April is now celebrated by the United Nations as the International Day of Human Space Flight.

fr.title: Le premier humain dans l'espace
fr.text: Youri Gagarine, de l'Union soviétique, devient le premier être humain à voyager dans l'espace, en faisant une fois le tour de la Terre à bord de Vostok 1.

ar.title: أول إنسان في الفضاء
ar.text: أصبح يوري غاغارين من الاتحاد السوفيتي أول إنسان يسافر إلى الفضاء، إذ دار حول الأرض مرة واحدة على متن المركبة فوستوك 1.

ko.title: 인류 최초의 우주 비행
ko.text: 소련의 유리 가가린이 보스토크 1호를 타고 지구를 한 바퀴 돌며 우주로 나간 최초의 인간이 되었습니다.

ja.title: 人類初の宇宙飛行
ja.text: ソ連のユーリイ・ガガーリンがボストーク1号で地球を1周し、宇宙へ行った最初の人間となりました。

zh.title: 人类首次进入太空
zh.text: 苏联的尤里·加加林乘坐东方1号绕地球飞行一圈,成为第一个进入太空的人类。

es.title: El primer ser humano en el espacio
es.text: Yuri Gagarin, de la Unión Soviética, se convirtió en el primer ser humano en viajar al espacio, dando una vuelta a la Tierra a bordo de la Vostok 1.

sw.title: Binadamu wa kwanza angani
sw.text: Yuri Gagarin wa Umoja wa Kisovieti akawa binadamu wa kwanza kusafiri angani, akizunguka Dunia mara moja ndani ya chombo Vostok 1.

en.title: The first World Cup final
en.text:
On 30 July 1930, in the brand-new Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 to win the first ever FIFA World Cup. Around 68,000 people watched in the stadium, and the next day was declared a national holiday in Uruguay.

The tournament was the dream of Jules Rimet, the French president of FIFA. Football had been played at the Olympic Games, and Uruguay had won the Olympic title in 1924 and 1928. In 1930 Uruguay was also celebrating 100 years of its first constitution, so it was chosen as host and promised to pay travel costs for visiting teams.

Even so, only 13 teams took part. Travelling from Europe meant weeks at sea, and only four European nations made the journey: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. Some of them sailed together on the same ship, the SS Conte Verde.

The first ever World Cup goal was scored by Lucien Laurent of France against Mexico on 13 July. The Estadio Centenario was not finished in time for the opening games because of heavy rain during construction.

The final was a fierce rivalry between neighbours. Each team wanted to use its own ball, so the first half was played with Argentina's ball and the second with Uruguay's. Argentina led 2–1 at half-time, but Uruguay scored three times in the second half.

From those small beginnings, the World Cup became the most watched sporting event on Earth. The 2026 tournament in North America is the first with 48 teams.

fr.title: La première finale de la Coupe du monde
fr.text: L'Uruguay bat l'Argentine 4–2 et devient le premier champion de la Coupe du monde de la FIFA.

ar.text: فازت الأوروغواي على الأرجنتين 4–2 لتصبح أول بطل لكأس العالم لكرة القدم.

ko.text: 우루과이가 아르헨티나를 4–2로 꺾고 FIFA 월드컵 초대 챔피언이 되었습니다.

ja.text: ウルグアイがアルゼンチンを4–2で破り、FIFAワールドカップ初代王者となりました。

zh.text: 乌拉圭以4–2击败阿根廷,成为首届国际足联世界杯冠军。

en.title: The World Cup comes to Africa
en.text:
On 11 June 2010, the FIFA World Cup kicked off for the first time on African soil. In Soccer City stadium in Johannesburg, the hosts South Africa played Mexico. When Siphiwe Tshabalala struck a beautiful goal for South Africa, the noise of tens of thousands of vuvuzelas filled the stadium. The match ended 1–1.

Africa had waited 80 years. African teams had long complained that the continent was overlooked, and South Africa had narrowly lost the vote for the 2006 tournament. In 2004 FIFA chose South Africa to host in 2010, only ten years after the end of apartheid.

Nelson Mandela, then 91, had campaigned for the bid. His presence at the final, waving to the crowd from a small cart, was one of the most emotional moments of the tournament.

The country built and upgraded stadiums, roads, airports and rail lines, including the Gautrain. Critics argued that the money could have been spent on housing and services, and that some stadiums would be little used afterwards, a debate that still continues.

On the field, South Africa became the first host nation to go out in the group stage, though it beat France. Ghana carried Africa's hopes into the quarter-finals, where they lost to Uruguay on penalties after a last-minute handball on the goal line denied them a winning goal.

Spain won the final against the Netherlands 1–0 with a goal by Andrés Iniesta. The tournament showed the world a confident, welcoming Africa and remains a source of pride across the continent.

fr.title: La Coupe du monde arrive en Afrique
fr.text: La Coupe du monde de la FIFA débute en Afrique du Sud, la première fois que le tournoi se déroule sur le continent africain.

ar.title: كأس العالم تصل إلى أفريقيا
ar.text: انطلقت بطولة كأس العالم لكرة القدم في جنوب أفريقيا، في أول مرة تُقام فيها البطولة على القارة الأفريقية.

es.text: La Copa Mundial de la FIFA comenzó en Sudáfrica, la primera vez que el torneo se celebró en el continente africano.

sw.text: Kombe la Dunia la FIFA lilianza nchini Afrika Kusini, ikiwa ni mara ya kwanza mashindano hayo kufanyika barani Afrika.

en.title: Filbert Bayi sets a world record
en.text:
On 2 February 1974, at the Commonwealth Games in Christchurch, New Zealand, a 20-year-old Tanzanian runner named Filbert Bayi did something experts said was impossible. He led the 1,500 metres from the very first stride, and kept running away from the world's best.

Most middle-distance races of the time were tactical: runners stayed together and sprinted at the end. Bayi ran differently. He went straight to the front and set a fierce pace, daring the others to keep up.

Behind him was a brilliant field, including New Zealand's John Walker and Kenya's Ben Jipcho. Walker closed in on the final straight, but Bayi held on. He crossed the line in 3 minutes 32.16 seconds, breaking the world record held for seven years by the American Jim Ryun. Walker, second, also ran under the old record. It is still remembered as one of the greatest 1,500-metre races ever run.

Bayi was born in 1953 near Karatu in northern Tanzania, and grew up running long distances at high altitude. He trained while serving in the Tanzania People's Defence Force.

In 1975 he broke the world record for the mile as well, running 3 minutes 51.0 seconds in Jamaica. Tanzania's boycott of the 1976 Montreal Olympics, in protest against apartheid sport links, kept him from a showdown there. In 1980 in Moscow he won Olympic silver in the 3,000-metre steeplechase.

Later he founded the Filbert Bayi Foundation and schools in Tanzania to support young athletes. His race in Christchurch remains a proud moment in Tanzanian and African sporting history.

fr.title: Filbert Bayi bat le record du monde
fr.text: Le coureur tanzanien Filbert Bayi remporte le 1 500 mètres aux Jeux du Commonwealth et établit un nouveau record du monde, en menant la course du début à la fin.

ar.title: فيلبرت باي يحطم الرقم القياسي العالمي
ar.text: فاز العدّاء التنزاني فيلبرت باي بسباق 1500 متر في ألعاب الكومنولث وسجّل رقمًا قياسيًا عالميًا جديدًا، متصدرًا السباق من البداية حتى النهاية.

ko.title: 필버트 바이, 세계 신기록 수립
ko.text: 탄자니아의 육상 선수 필버트 바이가 영연방 경기대회 1500m에서 처음부터 끝까지 선두를 지키며 우승하고 세계 신기록을 세웠습니다.

ja.title: フィルバート・バイが世界新記録

ja.text: タンザニアのランナー、フィルバート・バイがコモンウェルスゲームズの1500メートルでスタートからゴールまで先頭を走り続けて優勝し、世界新記録を樹立しました。

zh.title: 菲尔伯特·巴伊打破世界纪录
zh.text: 坦桑尼亚跑步运动员菲尔伯特·巴伊在英联邦运动会1500米比赛中从头领跑到尾夺冠,并创造了新的世界纪录。

es.title: Filbert Bayi bate el récord mundial
es.text: El atleta tanzano Filbert Bayi ganó los 1500 metros en los Juegos de la Mancomunidad y estableció un nuevo récord mundial, liderando la carrera de principio a fin.

sw.title: Filbert Bayi aweka rekodi ya dunia
sw.text: Mwanariadha wa Tanzania, Filbert Bayi, alishinda mbio za mita 1500 katika Michezo ya Jumuiya ya Madola na kuweka rekodi mpya ya dunia, akiongoza tangu mwanzo hadi mwisho.

en.title: The Titanic sinks
en.text:
At 11:40 p.m. on 14 April 1912, lookouts on the RMS Titanic saw an iceberg directly ahead. The ship turned, but too late. The iceberg scraped along the starboard side, opening several watertight compartments to the sea. In less than three hours, the largest ship in the world was gone.

Titanic was on her maiden voyage from Southampton in England to New York, with stops in France and Ireland. She was a symbol of wealth and modern engineering. About 2,224 people were on board, from millionaires in luxury suites to emigrants in third class hoping for a new life in America.

The ship carried lifeboats for only about 1,178 people, which was within the law of the time. Crew members were not fully trained to launch them, and many early boats left half empty. Third-class passengers, deep in the ship, had the hardest path to the boat deck.

At 2:20 a.m. on 15 April the ship broke apart and sank. More than 1,500 people died, most of them in the freezing water. The liner Carpathia, racing through the ice after hearing distress signals, rescued about 705 survivors later that morning.

The disaster led to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea in 1914. Ships were required to carry enough lifeboats for everyone, keep radio watch 24 hours a day, and the International Ice Patrol was created.

The wreck was found in 1985, about 3,800 metres deep, by a team led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel. Today it is protected as a memorial site.

fr.title: Le Titanic sombre
fr.text: Le grand paquebot Titanic sombre lors de son voyage inaugural après avoir heurté un iceberg. Plus de 1 500 personnes perdent la vie.

ar.title: غرق سفينة تيتانيك
ar.text: غرقت سفينة الركاب الضخمة تيتانيك في رحلتها الأولى بعد اصطدامها بجبل جليدي. ولقي أكثر من 1500 شخص حتفهم.

ko.title: 타이타닉호 침몰
ko.text: 대형 여객선 타이타닉호가 첫 항해 중 빙산과 충돌해 침몰했습니다. 1,500명이 넘는 사람이 목숨을 잃었습니다.

ja.title: タイタニック号が沈没
ja.text: 大型客船タイタニック号が処女航海中に氷山と衝突して沈没しました。1,500人以上が命を落としました。

zh.title: 泰坦尼克号沉没
zh.text: 大型客轮泰坦尼克号在处女航中撞上冰山后沉没,超过1500人遇难。

es.title: El Titanic se hunde
es.text: El gran transatlántico Titanic se hundió en su viaje inaugural tras chocar contra un iceberg. Más de 1500 personas perdieron la vida.

sw.title: Meli ya Titanic yazama
sw.text: Meli kubwa ya abiria, Titanic, ilizama katika safari yake ya kwanza baada ya kugonga jabali la barafu. Zaidi ya watu 1,500 walipoteza maisha.

en.title: The Great Pyramid of Giza is built
en.text:
Around 2560 BCE, workers in ancient Egypt completed the largest pyramid ever built, on the plateau of Giza beside the Nile. It was the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu, a king of the Fourth Dynasty. Today it is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

The pyramid was originally about 146 metres tall. For around 3,800 years it was the tallest human-made structure on Earth. It contains roughly 2.3 million blocks of stone, most of them limestone, some weighing several tonnes, with granite beams in the King's Chamber brought from Aswan, about 800 kilometres up the Nile.

It was once covered with polished white limestone casing stones that shone in the sun. Most of these were removed in later centuries and reused in buildings in Cairo.

For a long time people believed the pyramids were built by slaves. Archaeologists now know that the builders were organised teams of paid workers and skilled craftsmen. Near Giza they found a workers' town with bakeries, breweries, and cemeteries where workers were buried with honour.

In 2013, papyri were discovered at Wadi al-Jarf on the Red Sea coast. They include the logbook of an official named Merer, who described moving limestone blocks by boat along canals from the Tura quarries to Giza. They are the oldest inscribed papyri ever found.

Exactly how the stones were raised is still debated: ramps, levers and great skill all played a role. The Great Pyramid is aligned almost perfectly to the four compass points, a sign of the astronomy and mathematics of its builders.

sw.title: Piramidi Kuu ya Giza yajengwa
sw.text: Wafanyakazi wa Misri ya kale walikamilisha Piramidi Kuu ya Giza kama kaburi la Farao Khufu. Kwa zaidi ya miaka 3,800 ilikuwa jengo refu zaidi lililowahi kujengwa na binadamu.

en.title: Mansa Musa's journey to Mecca
en.place: Mali Empire to Cairo and Mecca
en.text:
In 1324 Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, set out on the hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca. His journey across the Sahara and through Cairo became one of the most famous travels of the Middle Ages, and made the wealth of West Africa known across the world.

Mali was founded in the 1230s by Sundiata Keita. By Musa's time it stretched from the Atlantic coast deep into the interior, controlling trade routes and the goldfields of Bambuk and Bure. Much of the gold used in North Africa and Europe came from West Africa.

Writers described a vast caravan, with thousands of people and camels carrying gold. When Musa reached Cairo, he and his followers spent and gave away so much gold that, according to the historian al-Umari who visited Cairo years later, the value of gold there was still lower than before.

Musa returned with scholars and architects, among them the Andalusian poet and architect Abu Ishaq al-Sahili. Under Musa, Timbuktu grew into a great centre of learning and trade. The Djinguereber Mosque there, built in his time, still stands.

Europe took notice. On the Catalan Atlas, made in 1375 in Majorca, Mansa Musa is painted sitting on a throne in West Africa, wearing a crown and holding a large gold nugget.

The Mali Empire declined in the fifteenth century and was overtaken by the Songhai Empire. But Mansa Musa's hajj remains a symbol of the wealth, faith and learning of medieval African kingdoms.

sw.title: Safari ya Mansa Musa kwenda Makka
sw.text: Mansa Musa, mtawala wa Dola ya Mali, alisafiri kwenda Makka akiwa na msafara mkubwa uliobeba dhahabu nyingi, kiasi kwamba safari yake ilijulikana kote Afrika, Mashariki ya Kati na Ulaya.

en.title: Ibn Battuta visits Kilwa
en.text:
Around 1331, the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta sailed down the East African coast and reached Kilwa, on an island off southern Tanzania. He wrote that Kilwa was one of the most beautiful and best-built towns in the world.

Ibn Battuta was born in Tangier in 1304. He set out on the hajj aged 21 and kept travelling for nearly 30 years, through North Africa, the Middle East, India, China, Mali and beyond. His travels, dictated later to the scholar Ibn Juzayy, are known as the Rihla.

Kilwa was at the height of its power. It was a Swahili city-state ruled by sultans, its stone houses and mosques built of coral rag and lime. It controlled much of the gold trade coming from the south, from Sofala in present-day Mozambique, gold that came from the kingdoms of the Zimbabwe plateau.

Merchants from Arabia, Persia and India came on the monsoon winds, trading cloth, beads and porcelain for gold, ivory and other goods. Kilwa minted its own copper coins.

Ibn Battuta praised the Sultan, al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman, known as Abu al-Mawahib, "father of gifts", for his generosity to scholars and the poor. The sultan built Husuni Kubwa, a huge palace on the cliffs, one of the largest buildings in sub-Saharan Africa at the time.

Kilwa was attacked by the Portuguese in 1505 and slowly declined. Today the ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and nearby Songo Mnara are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a reminder of the rich Swahili civilisation of the East African coast.

sw.title: Ibn Battuta azuru Kilwa
sw.text: Msafiri kutoka Morocco, Ibn Battuta, aliizuru Kilwa, mji tajiri wa biashara wa Waswahili kwenye pwani ya Afrika Mashariki, na akauelezea kuwa mmoja wa miji mizuri zaidi duniani.

en.title: Gutenberg's printing press
en.text:
Around 1440, a goldsmith from Mainz named Johannes Gutenberg began developing a new way to make books. His invention, a printing press using movable metal type, would change how knowledge spread across Europe and the world.

Before then, books in Europe were mostly copied by hand, often by monks, which took months or years for a single book. Woodblock printing existed, but carving a whole page into wood was slow.

Gutenberg's system combined several ideas. He cast individual letters in metal using a hand mould, so thousands of identical letters could be made and rearranged. He used an oil-based ink that stuck to metal, and adapted a screw press, like those used for wine and olives, to press paper evenly onto the inked type.

His most famous work is the Gutenberg Bible, printed around 1455. About 180 copies were made, and 49 survive today, some of the most valuable books in the world.

Printing was not new everywhere. In China, Bi Sheng made movable type from clay around 1040, and in Korea the Jikji, a Buddhist text printed with metal type in 1377, is the oldest surviving book made this way. But Gutenberg's press fitted the alphabets of Europe well and spread fast.

By 1500, printing presses were working in more than 250 European cities and millions of books had been printed. Cheap books fed the Renaissance, the Protestant Reformation and the Scientific Revolution, and helped ideas travel faster than any ruler could stop them.

sw.title: Mashine ya uchapishaji ya Gutenberg
sw.text: Johannes Gutenberg alibuni mashine ya uchapishaji yenye herufi za chuma zinazohamishika. Vitabu vikaweza kutengenezwa haraka na kwa bei nafuu, na maarifa yakaenea kwa kasi kuliko wakati wowote.

en.title: Vasco da Gama reaches the East African coast
en.text:
In July 1497 the Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama sailed from Lisbon with four ships, hoping to reach India by sea. In early 1498, after rounding the Cape of Good Hope, his fleet arrived on the East African coast.

What the Portuguese found surprised them. The Swahili coast was a world of wealthy trading towns: Mozambique Island, Kilwa, Mombasa, Malindi, Lamu and others. Stone mosques and houses lined the shore, and ships from Arabia, Persia, India and China called there. The Portuguese had come from a poorer corner of Europe into one of the richest trading systems on Earth.

At Mozambique Island and then at Mombasa, tensions quickly grew. In Mombasa, the Portuguese were received with suspicion, and fighting nearly broke out. They sailed on to Malindi, Mombasa's rival, where the sultan welcomed them and provided an experienced pilot who knew the monsoon winds of the Indian Ocean.

With his help, da Gama crossed to Calicut in India, arriving on 20 May 1498. The sea route from Europe to Asia was open.

For East Africa, the arrival was the start of a violent century. Portuguese fleets attacked Kilwa and Mombasa in 1505, demanding tribute and trying to control trade. In 1593 they built Fort Jesus in Mombasa, which still stands.

Swahili towns resisted, and in 1698 forces from Oman captured Fort Jesus, ending Portuguese power north of Mozambique. But the arrival of 1498 had begun the long age of European empires in the Indian Ocean.

sw.title: Vasco da Gama afika pwani ya Afrika Mashariki
sw.text: Mvumbuzi wa Kireno Vasco da Gama alizunguka Rasi ya Tumaini Jema na kufika Mombasa na Malindi akiwa njiani kwenda India — mwanzo wa ushawishi wa Wareno kwenye pwani ya Waswahili.

en.title: Zanzibar's slave market is closed
en.text:
On 5 June 1873, under heavy pressure from Britain, Sultan Barghash of Zanzibar signed a treaty that closed the great slave market of Zanzibar and banned the seaborne slave trade from his mainland ports.

In the nineteenth century, Zanzibar was the centre of the East African slave trade. Caravans travelled hundreds of kilometres into the interior, to places such as Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika and Tabora, buying and capturing people. Captives were forced to walk to the coast at Bagamoyo and Kilwa, often carrying ivory, and many died on the way.

On Zanzibar, enslaved people were sold in the open market, then sent to work on the island's clove plantations or shipped to Arabia, Persia and beyond. Historians estimate that hundreds of thousands of people passed through the trade in the nineteenth century alone.

Britain had abolished slavery in its own empire in 1833 and used its navy and its consul in Zanzibar, John Kirk, to push the Sultan. In 1873 the British threatened a naval blockade, and Barghash agreed.

On the site of the old market, the Anglican Christ Church Cathedral was built between 1873 and 1879. Its altar is said to stand where the whipping post once stood. Beside it, a memorial sculpture shows enslaved people in a pit, bound with real chains.

Closing the market did not end slavery at once. The legal status of slavery on Zanzibar was abolished only in 1897, and the practice continued illegally for years. The site is now a museum, a place to remember the millions of Africans whose lives were stolen by the slave trades.

sw.title: Soko la watumwa la Zanzibar lafungwa
sw.text: Kwa mkataba na Uingereza, Sultani Barghash alilifunga soko la watumwa la Zanzibar. Baadaye kanisa kuu lilijengwa mahali lilipokuwa soko hilo.

en.title: The Berlin Conference begins
en.text:
On 15 November 1884, representatives of 14 countries met in Berlin, invited by the German chancellor Otto von Bismarck. They came to agree on rules for European expansion in Africa. Not a single African was invited.

By the 1880s, European powers were racing to claim African land, a period later called the Scramble for Africa. Britain, France, Portugal, Germany and King Leopold II of Belgium all had ambitions, and they feared that rivalry over Africa could lead to war in Europe.

The conference lasted until 26 February 1885. Its General Act declared free trade in the Congo basin and on the Niger River, and recognised Leopold's claim to a vast area that became the Congo Free State, ruled as his personal property. Under Leopold, millions of Congolese suffered forced labour, mutilation and death in the rubber trade.

The conference also set the principle of "effective occupation": a European power claiming African territory had to notify the others and show that it controlled the area. This encouraged a rush of treaties, often signed under pressure or misunderstanding, and military expeditions.

The Berlin Conference did not draw every border in Africa, but it set the rules for the partition that followed. By 1914, almost the whole continent was under European rule. Only Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent.

Many of today's African borders were drawn in European capitals, cutting across peoples, kingdoms and trade routes. When the OAU was founded in 1963, African states chose to keep these borders to avoid conflict, but their legacy still shapes the continent.

sw.title: Mkutano wa Berlin waanza
sw.text: Mataifa ya Ulaya yalikutana Berlin kuweka kanuni za kugawana ardhi ya Afrika. Hakuna kiongozi wa Kiafrika aliyealikwa. Mkutano huo uliharakisha 'Kinyang'anyiro cha Afrika' cha kikoloni.

en.title: Victory at Adwa
en.text:
On 1 March 1896, in the mountains near the town of Adwa in northern Ethiopia, the army of Emperor Menelik II defeated an invading Italian army. It was the greatest victory of an African nation over a European colonial army in the age of empire.

The conflict began with a treaty. In 1889 Menelik and Italy signed the Treaty of Wuchale. The Amharic text of Article 17 said Ethiopia could use Italy to conduct its foreign affairs. The Italian text said it must. Italy claimed Ethiopia was now its protectorate. Menelik rejected the claim and later renounced the treaty.

Italy, which already held Eritrea, invaded. Menelik called on Ethiopians from every region to defend the country. Empress Taytu Betul, his wife, was a key strategist and commanded troops herself. Ethiopia had also bought modern rifles and artillery.

At Adwa, Italian general Oreste Baratieri divided his forces of about 17,000 to 18,000 men into columns that lost contact with each other in the rough terrain. The Ethiopian army, probably around 100,000 strong, attacked each column separately. By midday the Italians were routed, with around 6,000 killed and thousands captured.

In October 1896 the Treaty of Addis Ababa recognised Ethiopia's full independence. Ethiopia remained free while almost all of Africa was colonised.

Adwa became a symbol of African resistance and dignity. The green, yellow and red of Ethiopia's flag inspired the flags of many African nations after independence. The victory is celebrated in Ethiopia every year on 2 March, Adwa Victory Day, by the Ethiopian calendar.

sw.title: Ushindi wa Adwa
sw.text: Majeshi ya Ethiopia yakiongozwa na Mfalme Menelik II yalishinda jeshi la Italia huko Adwa. Ushindi huo ulilinda uhuru wa Ethiopia na ukawa alama ya upinzani wa Afrika dhidi ya ukoloni.

en.title: The Maji Maji uprising begins
en.text:
In July 1905, in the Matumbi Hills inland from Kilwa, farmers pulled up cotton plants from a German-run field. It was the first act of the Maji Maji uprising, one of the largest wars of resistance against colonial rule in Africa.

German East Africa had been under German control since the 1880s. Colonial officials forced people to grow cotton for export on communal plots, working for little or no pay, while their own food crops suffered. Taxes, forced labour and harsh treatment by local agents created deep anger.

A spiritual leader named Kinjikitile Ngwale, from Ngarambe, gave people a powerful message. He gave out sacred water, maji, and taught that it would protect warriors and turn German bullets to water. The water became a symbol that united many different peoples, including the Matumbi, Ngindo, Pogoro, Mbunga, Zaramo and Ngoni.

The uprising spread quickly across southern Tanganyika. Attacks targeted German posts, plantations and mission stations. Kinjikitile himself was captured and hanged early in the war.

The Germans responded with machine guns and a brutal scorched-earth policy, burning villages, fields and food stores. Famine killed far more people than the fighting. Historians estimate that between about 75,000 and 300,000 Africans died. In 1906 the Germans hanged many leaders at Songea, where the Maji Maji Memorial Museum stands today.

By 1907 the uprising was crushed. But it forced reforms in German colonial rule, and it became a powerful memory for Tanzanian nationalists. Julius Nyerere spoke of Maji Maji as an inspiration for the unity that later won independence.

sw.title: Vita vya Maji Maji vyaanza
sw.text: Jamii za kusini mwa Tanganyika ziliinuka dhidi ya utawala wa kikoloni wa Wajerumani na kilimo cha lazima cha pamba. Vita hivyo vilizimwa kufikia 1907, lakini vinakumbukwa kama moja ya mapambano makubwa dhidi ya ukoloni barani Afrika.

en.title: The Berlin Wall falls
en.text:
On the evening of 9 November 1989, crowds of East Germans gathered at the border crossings in Berlin. By midnight, guards had opened the gates. People streamed through, crying, laughing and climbing onto the Berlin Wall. The wall that had divided the city for 28 years had fallen.

After the Second World War, Germany was divided into a democratic West and a communist East. Berlin, deep inside East Germany, was also split. Millions of East Germans fled west through Berlin. To stop them, on 13 August 1961 the East German government began building a wall, which grew into a heavily guarded barrier more than 150 kilometres long around West Berlin.

Families were separated overnight. At least 140 people were killed trying to cross the wall in Berlin.

By 1989 the communist world was changing. Mikhail Gorbachev in the Soviet Union allowed more openness, Hungary opened its border with Austria, and huge peaceful protests filled the streets of East German cities.

On 9 November a government spokesman, Günter Schabowski, announced new travel rules at a press conference. Asked when they would start, he looked at his notes and said they applied immediately. The news spread on television. Crowds gathered at Bornholmer Straße, and at about 11:30 p.m. the officer in charge, unable to hold them back, opened the gate.

Within weeks, people were chipping pieces off the wall. Less than a year later, on 3 October 1990, Germany was reunited. The fall of the Berlin Wall became the symbol of the end of the Cold War.

sw.title: Ukuta wa Berlin waanguka
sw.text: Mamlaka ya Ujerumani Mashariki yalifungua vivuko vya mpaka katika Ukuta wa Berlin, na umati ukaanza kuubomoa. Ujerumani iliunganishwa tena chini ya mwaka mmoja baadaye.

en.title: The first farmers of the Fertile Crescent
en.text:
Around 11,500 years ago, in a band of land curving from the Nile valley through the Levant and southern Turkey down to the rivers of Iraq, people began to do something new. Instead of only gathering wild plants and hunting animals, they started planting seeds and keeping animals close. This change, often called the Neolithic Revolution, transformed human life more than almost anything before it.

The region is known as the Fertile Crescent. Wild wheat, barley, lentils and peas grew there naturally, along with wild sheep, goats, cattle and pigs. Over many generations, people chose the best seeds and the calmest animals, slowly creating domesticated crops and livestock.

At Göbekli Tepe in southern Turkey, people built huge carved stone pillars around 9500 BCE, before farming was fully established. Some archaeologists think gathering for great feasts at such places may have encouraged people to grow more food.

Farming allowed people to settle in villages such as Jericho and Çatalhöyük, store food, and support larger populations. It also brought new problems: hard labour, diseases spreading from animals, and arguments over land and stored wealth.

Farming was not invented in only one place. Over the following thousands of years it began independently in China (rice and millet), New Guinea, Mesoamerica (maize, beans and squash), the Andes (potatoes), and in Africa, where sorghum, pearl millet, yams and African rice were domesticated, and cattle herding spread across the Sahara when it was green.

Almost every city, kingdom and invention that came later was built on the food surplus that farming made possible.

en.title: Writing is invented in Sumer
en.text:
Around 3200 BCE, in the city of Uruk in southern Mesopotamia, scribes pressed marks into wet clay with reed pens. They were keeping records of grain, beer, sheep and workers. Out of these simple accounts grew one of humanity's greatest inventions: writing.

Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers in today's Iraq, was home to the Sumerians, who built some of the first cities. Uruk may have had more than 40,000 people. Running temples and storehouses for so many needed a way to remember who owed what.

The earliest signs were pictures: a jar, a head of grain, an ox. Over centuries they became wedge-shaped marks, which we call cuneiform, from the Latin word for wedge. Signs came to stand for sounds as well as things, so scribes could write names, laws, letters, prayers and stories.

Cuneiform was used for about 3,000 years and adapted for many languages, including Akkadian, Babylonian, Assyrian and Hittite. Hundreds of thousands of clay tablets survive, because clay hardens when baked, and libraries burned in wars actually preserved their tablets.

Writing was invented separately in other places too: Egyptian hieroglyphs appeared at almost the same time, Chinese writing by about 1200 BCE, and the Maya and other peoples of Mesoamerica developed their own scripts.

Writing allowed laws to be fixed, history to be recorded, and stories like the Epic of Gilgamesh to survive thousands of years. It marks the boundary between what historians call prehistory and history.

en.title: The Code of Hammurabi
en.text:
Around 1754 BCE, King Hammurabi of Babylon set up a tall black stone pillar carved with nearly 300 laws. At the top, a carving shows the king standing before Shamash, the sun god and god of justice. The Code of Hammurabi is one of the oldest and most complete written law collections in the world.

Hammurabi ruled from about 1792 to 1750 BCE. Through war and diplomacy he united much of Mesopotamia under Babylon. Publishing laws helped show that the king ruled justly and brought order to his many peoples.

The laws cover everyday life: trade and prices, loans and debt, farming and irrigation, marriage and divorce, inheritance, adoption, theft, building work and medical care. One law says that if a builder's house collapses and kills its owner, the builder shall be put to death.

Some punishments follow the rule of "an eye for an eye": if a man destroys another man's eye, his own eye shall be destroyed. But the laws were not equal for everyone. Punishments differed for nobles, ordinary free people and enslaved people.

Hammurabi was not the first lawgiver. Earlier codes, such as that of Ur-Nammu around 2100 BCE, existed. But his stele is the best preserved. It was carried off as war booty to Susa in Iran in the twelfth century BCE, where French archaeologists found it in 1901. Today it stands in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

The idea that laws should be written down and known to all, rather than kept only in the mind of the ruler, is a foundation of legal systems today.

en.title: The Kushite kings rule Egypt
en.text:
Around 747 BCE, King Piye of Kush marched north from his capital at Napata, in today's Sudan, and conquered Egypt. For nearly a century, kings from Kush ruled both lands as the Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt, sometimes called the Black Pharaohs.

Kush lay along the Nile south of Egypt, in the region called Nubia. It was one of Africa's earliest great kingdoms, rich in gold, ivory, ebony and skilled archers. For centuries Egypt had controlled Nubia, but as Egypt split into rival states, Kush grew strong.

Piye recorded his campaign on a great stone stela. He presented himself as a devoted follower of the god Amun, restoring order to a divided Egypt. He was famous for loving horses and punishing a defeated ruler for letting his horses go hungry.

His successors, including Shabaqo and Taharqa, ruled from Memphis and Thebes. Taharqa built temples across Egypt and Nubia. The Kushite kings revived old Egyptian traditions, and also built pyramids for their own tombs, a custom that Egypt itself had long abandoned.

In the 660s BCE the Assyrians drove the Kushites out of Egypt. Kush continued for another thousand years, later with its capital at Meroë, where more than 200 pyramids stand today, more than in all of Egypt. Meroë was a centre of iron-working, and its people developed their own script, Meroitic, which scholars still cannot fully read.

Kush shows that ancient Africa had powerful kingdoms that shaped the history of the Nile and the whole ancient world.

en.title: The Buddha's teaching begins
en.text:
Around the fifth century BCE, a man named Siddhartha Gautama sat in meditation beneath a tree at Bodh Gaya in northern India. According to Buddhist tradition, there he reached enlightenment, a complete understanding of suffering and how to end it. He became known as the Buddha, "the awakened one".

Siddhartha was born into a ruling family in Lumbini, in today's Nepal. Tradition says he grew up in comfort, protected from hardship, until he saw an old man, a sick man, a dead body and a wandering holy man. Troubled, he left his palace to search for the meaning of suffering.

He tried extreme fasting and self-punishment, but found that this did not bring wisdom. Instead he taught a Middle Way between luxury and harsh denial.

He gave his first sermon in a deer park at Sarnath, near Varanasi. He taught the Four Noble Truths: life includes suffering; suffering comes from craving; it can end; and the way to end it is the Noble Eightfold Path, including right understanding, right speech, right action and right mindfulness.

The Buddha taught for about 45 years, welcoming people of every social class, including women, into his community of monks and nuns. Scholars debate the exact dates of his life.

In the third century BCE, the Indian emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism and sent missionaries far and wide. Buddhism spread to Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia, China, Korea, Japan and Tibet. Today hundreds of millions of people follow it, and ideas such as mindfulness meditation have spread around the world.

en.title: Democracy begins in Athens
en.text:
In 508 BCE, a leader named Cleisthenes introduced reforms in the Greek city of Athens that gave power to the ordinary citizens. The system came to be called demokratia, from the Greek words demos, the people, and kratos, power.

Before this, Athens had been ruled by aristocrats and tyrants. Cleisthenes reorganised citizens into ten new tribes that mixed people from the city, the coast and the countryside, breaking the power of old noble families.

The heart of Athenian democracy was the Assembly, which met on a hill called the Pnyx. Any male citizen could attend, speak and vote on war, peace, laws and taxes. Thousands came. A Council of 500, chosen by lot, prepared business. Many officials were chosen by lottery, not elections, so that ordinary citizens shared in government.

Athens even had ostracism: once a year citizens could write a name on a broken piece of pottery, and the person with the most votes, if enough were cast, was sent away for ten years. It was a way to stop anyone becoming too powerful.

But Athenian democracy was limited. Women, enslaved people and foreigners living in Athens could not vote. Only a minority of adults were full citizens.

Democracy in Athens survived, with interruptions, for nearly two centuries, a period when the city also produced great drama, philosophy and architecture, including the Parthenon. Its ideas, that the people should rule and that leaders must answer to citizens, inspired later democratic movements around the world.

en.title: Qin Shi Huang unites China
en.text:
In 221 BCE, King Zheng of the state of Qin completed the conquest of his last rival and united China under one ruler. He gave himself a new title, Shi Huangdi, the First Emperor.

For more than two centuries, China had been divided among warring states. Qin, in the west, built a strong army and a strict system of laws under the philosophy known as Legalism, which held that people must be controlled by clear rewards and harsh punishments.

The First Emperor worked to make his huge empire one. He standardised weights, measures and coins, the width of cart axles so wagons could use the same roads, and above all the written script, so that people speaking different languages could read the same documents. That shared writing system helped hold China together for the next two thousand years.

He built roads and canals, and joined and extended earlier walls in the north into a long defensive line, an early form of the Great Wall. Hundreds of thousands of labourers worked on these projects, and many died.

He was also feared. His government is said to have burned books it considered dangerous and punished scholars who criticised it.

When he died in 210 BCE, he was buried in a vast tomb near Xi'an guarded by the Terracotta Army: thousands of life-size clay soldiers, each with a different face, discovered by farmers digging a well in 1974.

The Qin dynasty collapsed soon after his death, but the Han dynasty that followed kept the unified empire he had created. The word China itself may come from Qin.

en.title: King Ezana of Aksum adopts Christianity
en.text:
In the fourth century CE, King Ezana of Aksum, in today's northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, became a Christian. His kingdom became one of the first states in the world to adopt Christianity, and the church he supported, now the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, has continued ever since.

Aksum was one of the great powers of the ancient world. A Persian writer of the third century listed it with Rome, Persia and China as one of the four great kingdoms. Its port of Adulis on the Red Sea traded ivory, gold, incense and other goods with Egypt, Arabia, India and the Roman world.

Aksum minted its own coins in gold, silver and bronze, one of very few ancient African states to do so. Its kings built giant stone obelisks, or stelae, to mark royal tombs. The tallest still standing is about 24 metres high, carved to look like a multi-storey building.

According to tradition, a young Christian from Tyre named Frumentius was shipwrecked and brought to the Aksumite court, where he educated the young Ezana. Frumentius later became the first bishop of Aksum. Ezana's coins show the change: early ones carry the crescent and disc of older gods, later ones the cross.

Aksum also developed the Ge'ez script, which is still used for the Amharic and Tigrinya languages today.

Aksum declined from the seventh century as trade routes changed. But it laid the foundations for the Christian kingdoms of Ethiopia, with their unique churches, manuscripts and traditions, including the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela built centuries later.

en.title: The last Western Roman emperor is deposed
en.text:
